newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK CBANK SETS NO REPO TENDER ON FRIDAY.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK CBANK SETS NO REPO TENDER ON FRIDAY.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said in a statement it would not hold any refinancing repo tender on Friday.
The statement gave no further details and NBS officials were not immediately available for comment on the decision.
The central bank monitors market liquidity daily and decides each morning whether to hold any open market operations.
The fulfilment of minimum reserves requirement by commercial banks is one of the main NBS's yardstick for assessing money market liquidity.
According to NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector as of August 7 exceeded by 0.03 percent the cumulative volume of funds needed to meet minimum reserves requirements later this month.
The daily volume of minimum reserves for commercial banks totals 36.817 billion crowns in the current reserves period ending August 15.

The latest NBS repo operation was a one-week refinancing repo tender on Wednesday when the central bank added 2.0 billion crowns at an average rate of 18.17 percent, down from 18.32 percent in similar repo on Tuesday.
Slovak money market dealers said no significant liquidity inflows and outflows were expected on Friday. Overnight rates opened at around 27 percent.
